prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and the identification of its active form, which laid the foundation for incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: a single-part B001 prize to Holst, Drucker and Mojsov. After the full first round I still ground it in the science. Holst established in humans that GLP-1 is a glucose-dependent incretin and that its secretion explains part of the incretin effect, Mojsov identified and synthesised the biologically active GLP-1(7-36) form, and Drucker defined the proglucagon-derived peptide biology and the therapeutic concept. That chain has been confirmed by many independent laboratories and by large randomised trials in glycaemia, weight, and cardiovascular and renal outcomes, so maturity is not in doubt. The chair's questions did not produce a stronger competing case. B045 and B043 each have a real attribution or maturity gap that B001 does not share to the same degree. From an autoimmunity and clinical perspective I also value that this is a discovery whose mechanism has been tested in patients at scale, which is the strongest form of confirmation a physiology or medicine prize can cite.
statement.case_against: Attribution remains the weakness and I should not soften it. Mojsov's priority for the active peptide relative to the Habener group is not settled by the supplied record, and the identification point is the part of the citation I am least able to verify independently. Omitting Knudsen is a genuine cost: her long-acting analogue work is what turned the physiology into the drugs, and a three-name basic-science prize can be read as under-crediting development. A further risk is that a prize with this public profile is judged on the visibility of the drugs rather than on the discovery, which is why the citation must be anchored on physiology and the identity of the peptide.

responses.point: The chair's questions ask whether the committee can resolve the early peptide-identification priority from primary evidence, and whether a three-name B001 without Knudsen is acceptable.
responses.response: I cannot resolve the priority question from the files supplied, and I will not pretend recollection is evidence. What I recall is that the cloning of proglucagon cDNA and the demonstration that the truncated GLP-1(7-36) peptide, not the full-length sequence, is the insulinotropic form were distinct steps, and Mojsov's contribution sits in the second. That is why I keep her in the trio but word the citation around identification of the active form and not around first discovery of the sequence. On Knudsen, I accept the omission as an explicit judgement that this prize rewards physiology and identity. I would state that in the committee record so it is not mistaken for a finding that development is lesser. I would only change the trio if documented evidence showed the active-form identification was substantially made elsewhere.

responses.point: Linnarsson would narrow B045 to June and Sadelain and regards the Eshhar and Gross gap as serious, while noting that a drug-framed prize risks reading as a product award.
responses.response: I agree that the missing chimeric receptor originators are the main obstacle to B045, and dropping Rosenberg does not repair it. Where I differ slightly is that I would not treat a June and Sadelain pair as a stable endpoint, because the first-generation receptor work would still be uncredited. That keeps B045 an alternative for me and not a lead candidate. Your point about a product award is the reason I want the B001 citation to name the hormone's physiology, not a drug or a drug class.

responses.point: Perlmann notes that if the credit questions on B001 cannot be settled, B043 or B045 may be easier to defend, and asks whether a two-part configuration is preferable to a single achievement.
responses.response: I take the point that B043 has the cleanest attribution on the list (Mori and Walter), and it is why I keep it as an alternative. But I do not think unresolved credit questions on B001 are severe enough to switch, because the three credited names map onto three distinct, documented contributions. A two-part B001 plus B043 would force a reduction of the GLP-1 trio, and I do not see a principled name to drop. The clinical consequences of the unfolded protein response are still emerging, so I would hold B043 for a later year rather than pair it now.

responses.point: Sandberg says that limited translation does not disqualify B043 and that the GLP-1 priority dispute is not independently verified.
responses.response: I agree that limited translation alone does not disqualify a basic mechanism, and I would be comfortable with B043 on its merits as a future prize. My concern this year is relative: B001 has both the mechanism and decades of independent human outcome evidence, so the comparison is between a very mature, population-scale discovery and a mechanism whose disease relevance is still being defined. Your caution that the priority dispute is unverified is shared by every member, and I read it as a reason for careful citation wording, not as a reason to demote the achievement.

responses.point: El-Manira says that reading the credit as basic science versus industrial development is a judgement and not a finding, and that long-term safety of chronic therapy is still being characterised.
responses.response: I agree that it is a judgement, and I would keep it labelled that way in the committee record. On chronic safety, I accept it is not fully characterised, but the randomised outcome data are broad enough that it does not bear on the discovery itself, which is what the citation honours. I would not let it move B001 down, though it is a fair reason to avoid wording the citation around a particular therapeutic.

uncertainties: Priority for the active GLP-1 peptide among Mojsov, the Habener group and others cannot be settled from the supplied record, and my account rests on recollection.
Whether the committee accepts omitting Knudsen as an explicit discovery-versus-development judgement, which would change the laureate set if reversed.
Whether the B045 originator gap (Eshhar, Gross) can be closed under the three-person cap.
Whether the disease relevance of the unfolded protein response (B043) matures enough to make it a stronger candidate in a later year.
statement.conflict_note: No change from round 1. I have no documented personal or institutional connection to the credited GLP-1, CAR-T or unfolded protein response names. A shared Karolinska Institutet setting or field alone does not establish a conflict. I note the round-1 disclosures by other members and see no relationship to any credited name that would require my recusal.
